The problem manifested only when _source was asked for explicitly. I am not too happy with not returning any error and simply skipping the _source part of the request, I would have rather thrown an error there. Thoughts?

rename.from: NPE when querying an index with _source diabled and _source field
rename.to: NPE when fetching source from an index with _source disabled

body:
> The problem manifested only when _source was asked for explicitly. I am not too happy with not returning any error and simply skipping the _source part of the request, I would have rather thrown an error there. Thoughts?

I hate to say that but I think it should be configurable on a per request basis? When querying multiple indices you might want to return `foo` for some docs and `bar` for other docs while searching on a third field. And sometimes you query well defined indices and a missing source field must just throw an error in that case.

@tlrx what should be configurable? The behaviour? Either throw an error or skip without barfing? I am afraid I don't follow why skipping some part of the request that cannot be performed would help. You are going to run into problems when reading the response anyway as some part will be missing.
In my case, _source is disabled but some fields are still stored. So it is definitely still possible to retrieve some fields event though _source is disabled.

@marfago then you should use `fields` rather than `_source`. `_source` will always try to extract fields out of the source field and will return only those rather than the whole source. Fields will instead get the stored fields from lucene directly. Not sure whether the spark integration supports any of this.

@javanna thank you for the clarification. 
What if:
1)keep as default the current behaviour, just handling/wrapping the NPE with a more meaningful message/exception 
2)introduce a boolean query parameter (a sort of ignore_disabled_source) in order to change behaviour and silently ignore indexes with disabled _source
3)open a new issue in elasticsearch-spark for handling the "fields" parameter.

issue.title: Support querying indexes with _source disabled

repository.name: elasticsearch-hadoop
repository.description: :elephant: Elasticsearch real-time search and analytics natively integrated with Hadoop

issue.body:
### Feature description

Looks like the current implementation of elasticsearch-spark library does not support querying indexes with _source disabled.
In particular take a look #https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/20408 and [SearchRequestBuilder.java](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-hadoop/blob/bbafa1478bfad9b374696e26c9a4c5521678dd6e/mr/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/hadoop/rest/SearchRequestBuilder.java#L183).

If _source is disabled in the index mapping and some fields are still specified in the query, the "fields" parameter should be used instead.

body:
> 1)keep as default the current behaviour, just handling/wrapping the NPE with a more meaningful message/exception 

the current behaviour after the fix is "ignore the _source parameter if _source is disabled", I don't like that

> 2)introduce a boolean query parameter (a sort of ignore_disabled_source) in order to change behaviour and silently ignore indexes with disabled _source

I tend to be against this, I don't think it is worth adding yet another request parameter for such an edge case, in the spirit of #11172.

> 3)open a new issue in elasticsearch-spark for handling the "fields" parameter.

thanks for doing that ;)

> I tend to be against this, I don't think it is worth adding yet another request parameter for such an edge case, in the spirit of #11172.

This is a very good point @javanna and the rationale behind #11172 is good too. I agree we should throw an error here but I'd like to be sure how we handle similar case with `fields` or `stored_fields`.
thanks Tanguy, maybe @clintongormley has some opinion too on this
++ to what @javanna said. If you disable source and you use a feature that needs it you fail. Hard!

@javanna and @s1monw In my use case (see the description), the first query succeeds returning an apparently valid scrollId, then the second query fails because the _source is disabled. 
I think it should fail earlier, preventing the scrollId to be created.
